title: MCP Catalog admin — add, edit, and remove catalog entries from the dashboard

steps.caption: The MCP Catalog administrative interface lives at Settings → MCP resources → MCP catalog sources — restricted strictly to OpenShift AI administrators; regular users see the entries but cannot change them.

details.label: Location
details.value: Settings → MCP resources → MCP catalog sources

details.label: Sources
details.value: Community · Red Hat · Red Hat Partner MCP Servers

steps.caption: Add source — the YAML-based creation flow that previously required a hand-edited Kubernetes ConfigMap, with form validation and no cluster CLI round-trip.

details.label: Fields
details.value: Name · YAML file · Server filters · Enable source

details.label: Enable source
details.value: checked — keep it disabled to hide servers while authoring

steps.caption: Each source is a YAML file: an optional source label and an mcp_servers list — the same style as the Model Catalog administrative interface, so skills transfer between them.
Author the entry as YAML — add multiple servers under mcp_servers to publish a bundle from one source file; server names appear in the catalog preview after upload.

details.label: Tools
details.value: read-only toolsets with named access types

steps.caption: MCP catalog preview — complete all required fields, then click Preview to see which servers will appear in the catalog: 2 of 2 MCP servers included.
Add — the Workshop MCP servers source appears in the list and validation reports honest status (Starting) while the operator reconciles the catalog source configuration.

The payoff from the developer's point of view: the Prometheus and Kubernetes servers appear in the AI Hub MCP Catalog (Other MCP servers) — the discovery surface developers browse when deploying MCP servers.

details.label: Catalog
details.value: AI hub → MCP servers (Other MCP servers)

steps.caption: Edit — open the source from the list: the YAML and the catalog preview load prefilled; changes apply to the catalog source configuration without touching any ConfigMap resource.

details.label: Server filters
details.value: optional filters limit which servers appear

steps.caption: Update the YAML and save — the form detects the change and asks to refresh the preview; the operator applies it without a cluster CLI round-trip.

details.label: Form banner
details.value: Source configuration changed. Refresh the preview.

steps.caption: Saved — validation status Ready. From your side no ConfigMap was touched: the interface performed the configuration changes for you.

details.label: From your side
details.value: no ConfigMap touched — the interface performed the change

steps.caption: Remove — deleting a source requires typed confirmation; the entry and its servers disappear from the AI Hub MCP Catalog. Coordinate with your team before deleting entries others are browsing.

details.label: Effect
details.value: servers removed from the MCP catalog

details.label: Cleanup
details.value: catalog source configuration cleaned up for you

steps.caption: The lifecycle is complete — add, edit, and remove with guided dialogs; the only oc apply in this workshop is the old-way ConfigMap contrast the interface replaces.

details.label: Round trip
details.value: the old-way oc apply — the contrast
